title: fastify 5.10.0 has known vulnerabilities relevant to this app's trustProxy:true config
description: Found while installing @fastify/swagger for canvas-lfc's foundation (unrelated to that work -- pre-existing, confirmed via 'git diff package-lock.json' showing fastify's own resolved version (5.10.0) was untouched by that install). npm audit reports fastify <=5.12.0 has two advisories: (1) GHSA-w2qp-rph6-63g4, schema validation bypass via root primitive coercion mismatch; (2) GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2, X-Forwarded-* spoofing under trustProxy hop-count -- directly relevant here, since apps/api/src/app.ts explicitly sets trustProxy: true (needed for Azure App Service's TLS-terminating reverse-proxy topology, see that line's own comment).
acceptance_criteria: fastify bumped to a patched >=5.13.0-ish version (check the advisory for the exact fixed version at fix time) via npm audit fix (non-breaking within the same major) or a manual package.json bump. Full apps/api test suite green after the bump, since Fastify major-adjacent point releases have occasionally changed validation/routing edge-case behavior this app's own tests would catch.
notes: Not fixed in this pass -- found and disclosed while doing unrelated work (canvas-lfc/OpenAPI wiring), deliberately not silently bundled into that PR.

title: Live-verify RP-Initiated Logout fix (canvas-252) against real deployed Keycloak
description: canvas-252's fix (RP-Initiated OIDC logout: session.ts's /auth/logout now returns a logoutUrl for SSO sessions, AppShell.tsx navigates the browser there, Keycloak realm config + deploy.sh reconciliation now set post.logout.redirect.uris) is implemented and covered by unit/contract tests (apps/api 354/354 +1 skipped), but was never verified against a REAL deployed Keycloak instance -- canvas-rg was mid-destroy when the fix landed, so this is genuinely untested live. canvas-252's own acceptance criteria explicitly called for live verification ('matching this project's own established confirmed live, not just unit tests precedent for auth-flow changes'), which this bead exists to close out.
acceptance_criteria: Next time canvas-rg is deployed (deploy.sh) or already running: sign in via SSO, click Sign Out, then click Sign in with SSO again -- confirm a REAL Keycloak credential prompt appears (not a silent bounce-back into the app as the same user). Also confirm a local-auth-only session (if ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH is ever true on that deployment) still gets a plain, instant sign-out with no Keycloak round-trip. If it fails, check first that infra/keycloak/CanvasRealm-realm.json's/deploy.sh's post.logout.redirect.uris actually reconciled onto the real client (a live Keycloak admin-console check of the canvas-api client's 'Post logout redirect URIs' field is a fast way to confirm).
notes: Filed instead of closing canvas-252 outright, per explicit instruction to leave a bead open for this. Also saved as a bd remember so a future session proactively raises it the next time the Azure environment is spun up (deploy.sh/resume.sh).

title: Port Canvas's multi-diagram-type capability into ADP (additive to existing C4 workspace)
description: Follow-up to canvas-hly's feasibility study (docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md, Part 2). Driver: ADP has grown from a Solution-Architect-focused tool into a broader Enterprise/Business Architecture tool, and its C4-only diagramming (React Flow + Structurizr DSL, ElementKind stops at component level) is now too limiting for that scope. Unlike a full replace/merge (Part 1, not feasible -- conflicting source-of-truth models), porting the 5 non-C4 diagram families (flowchart, sequence, ERD, UML, cloud-architecture) is genuinely feasible as an ADDITIVE capability: these have no existing ADP typed-model representation to conflict with, so DSL-as-truth (packages/diagram-core) can simply be adopted for them with zero tension against ArchitectureDescription/adp.store, which stays completely untouched. Two facts verified directly (not assumed): packages/diagram-core has exactly 2 runtime deps (yaml, @dagrejs/dagre), both pure JS, no server coupling -- directly consumable from a browser bundle; ADP's web/ already runs the same toolchain generation as canvas's apps/web (React 18, TS 5.x, Vite, Vitest, Playwright).
design: Phased approach: (1) vendor/publish packages/diagram-core into ADP web/, confirm it builds and its existing test suite runs clean there -- pure spike, no product surface yet. (2) New, independent backend table + minimal FastAPI CRUD router in ADP for the new diagram types' DSL content -- additive only, ArchitectureDescription/adp.store untouched. (3) Port canvas's React canvas-editing components (apps/web/src/canvas/) into ADP's web/src/canvas/, alongside (not replacing) C4Canvas.tsx -- ADP's canvas view gains a diagram-type picker; C4 keeps its existing typed-model pipeline exactly as today. (4) Stretch/later, separately scoped: governance/permissions reconciliation between canvas's admin Standards system and ADP's own RBAC (enterprise_architect/solution_architect/technical_architect/reviewer); linking new diagrams to ADP's traceability model; AI chat integration (canvas's AI-chat tool-calling system is wired to its own provider config/tool surface, distinct from ADP's own LangGraph intake/recommendation/validation pipeline -- explicitly out of scope for a first port). Rendering/export for the new types uses canvas's own SVG renderer directly (pure TS) -- adp.renderer's Python/Structurizr pipeline stays C4-only, untouched. Auth needs no new work -- both already use Keycloak OIDC (infra/azure/README.md already documents this alignment).
acceptance_criteria: Two open product decisions need real answers before implementation starts, not assumptions: (a) is deferring governance/standards-enforcement on the new diagram types acceptable for v1 (recommended: yes, defer); (b) are these new diagrams attached to an ADP Design (part of an EA deliverable) or fully standalone artifacts independent of any design -- this changes the new table's shape. Phase 1 (vendor + build/test spike) should be completed and verified before phases 2-3 are scoped in detail.
notes: Execution moves to ADP's own repo/tracker (/home/jmuir/projects/ADP), using its own speckit setup and its own beads database -- per the user's explicit direction to leave Canvas as a standalone diagram tool, untouched by this effort. This canvas-side bead stays open as the cross-repo reference/pointer to docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md's Part 2 analysis (the phased plan, the two verified portability facts, and the two open product decisions) -- the actual spec/plan/tasks/implementation work will be tracked in ADP's own specs/ and beads, not here.

title: Mermaid DSL full-compliance roadmap (diagram-type by diagram-type)
description: Syntax audit against the full Mermaid language reference (https://mermaid.ai/open-source/intro/syntax-reference.html) found real gaps across every diagram-core parser, beyond what feature 002 (US5) scoped in. This epic tracks the overall roadmap; work is deliberately split into separate bounded spec-kit features (like 001/002 before it) and interspersed with unrelated feature work rather than done as one continuous push. See child issues for the per-family breakdown.
design: Canvas supports 6 of Mermaid's ~30 diagram types: flowchart, sequence, class/UML, ER, C4, architecture (cloud infra). The other ~24 (state, gantt, pie, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, kanban, journey, quadrant, sankey, XY chart, block, packet, requirement, ZenUML, radar, treemap, venn, Ishikawa, Wardley, Cynefin, treeview, swimlanes, event modeling) are entirely unimplemented — this was an explicit 001 spec decision, not an oversight, but is included here for roadmap completeness.

title: Enrich OpenAPI route schemas for richer Swagger docs (request/response bodies, tags)
description: The OpenAPI/Swagger wiring (apps/api/src/docs/api-docs.routes.ts, gated behind ENABLE_API_DOCS) lists every real route (Fastify's own introspection needs no per-route schema for that), but request/response bodies, params, and tags stay undocumented until individual routes opt into Fastify's schema option. Adding that across all ~16 *.routes.ts files' worth of endpoints (47 total) is a much larger, separate pass than the foundational wiring itself -- deliberately not attempted in that pass.
acceptance_criteria: A meaningful subset (or all) of the 47 routes gain a Fastify schema (body/params/querystring/response, tags grouping by resource) so /docs shows real, browsable request/response shapes instead of just path+method. Each route's schema.security should reference the existing cookieAuth scheme where the route actually requires auth (most of them).
notes: Foundational wiring (this session): apps/api/src/docs/api-docs.routes.ts, config.ts's enableApiDocs, app.ts's early registration. Verified live: /docs/json correctly lists all 47 routes.

title: Template import: other C4 levels (Container/Component/Deployment)
description: Follow-up to canvas-73s (Template import: C4 Context foundation). Extend the C4 template-import pattern to Container/Component/Deployment levels -- can reuse c4-context-template-compiler.ts's alias-generation/collision logic almost directly; only the section shape and relationship rules change per level (Container/Component allow entity-to-entity relationships, unlike Context's Level-1 hub-and-spoke restriction). One doc + one TemplateCompiler per level (or one doc covering all three, given how similar their grammar is), registered under diagramTypeId 'c4-container'/'c4-component'/'c4-deployment'.

title: Template import: UML class diagram
description: Follow-up to canvas-73s (Template import: C4 Context foundation). Author a Markdown intake-template doc (matching docs/c4-context-template.md's style) for the UML class diagram family, plus a TemplateCompiler registered under diagramTypeId 'uml'. Natural content shape: classes with member bodies (attributes/methods, visibility, static/abstract) + relationships (inheritance/composition/aggregation/association/dependency/realization/link/lollipop) with cardinality labels.

title: Template import: Architecture family (network/deployment/cloud-infrastructure)
description: Follow-up to canvas-73s (Template import: C4 Context foundation). Author a Markdown intake-template doc (matching docs/c4-context-template.md's style) for the architecture-beta family, plus a TemplateCompiler registered under diagramTypeId(s) covering network/deployment/cloud-infrastructure (all share dslFamily 'architecture'). Natural content shape: services (with vendor icon refs) + groups/junctions (nestable) + directional edges with anchors.

title: Template import: ERD
description: Follow-up to canvas-73s (Template import: C4 Context foundation). Author a Markdown intake-template doc (matching docs/c4-context-template.md's style) for the ER diagram family, plus a TemplateCompiler registered under diagramTypeId 'erd'. Natural content shape: entities with attribute blocks (type/name/PK/FK/UK) + relationships with two-sided crow's-foot cardinality and a mandatory label.

title: Template import: Sequence diagram
description: Follow-up to canvas-73s (Template import: C4 Context foundation). Author a Markdown intake-template doc (matching docs/c4-context-template.md's style: numbered sections, tables, type legend, mapping reference, worked example) for the sequence diagram family, plus a TemplateCompiler implementation registered in packages/diagram-core/src/template/template-registry.ts under diagramTypeId 'sequence'. Natural content shape: participants/actors (declaration order) + an ordered list of messages, optionally with activate/deactivate and loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break blocks.

title: deploy.sh's own printed canvas-keycloak-users invocation doesn't work as documented
description: Two real gaps found during a live first-ever canvas Azure deploy (2026-09-08): (1) deploy.sh's confirmation prompt (read -r -p "Proceed with deployment? [y/N]") aborts silently with exit 1 when run non-interactively/no stdin -- no error explaining why, just 'Aborted.'. (2) The exact invocation deploy.sh prints at the end for provisioning real users -- 'az containerapp job start --name canvas-keycloak-users --resource-group canvas-rg --env-vars KC_USERS=...' -- fails on the installed az CLI/containerapp extension version: passing --env-vars without --image/--command/--args causes the CLI to require a full container override, which drops the job's own command/args (node infra/keycloak/create-users.mjs), so the container instead boots the API server's default entrypoint and crashes on a missing DATABASE_URL. Worked around live by also passing --image/--command/--args and the job's other original env vars (KEYCLOAK_URL/KEYCLOAK_REALM/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD via secretref:) alongside KC_USERS.
acceptance_criteria: deploy.sh's own printed post-deploy instructions for canvas-keycloak-users (and ideally canvas-seed/canvas-migrate too, if they'd hit the same gap) actually work when copy-pasted verbatim on a current az CLI/containerapp extension. Confirmation prompt either accepts a --yes/non-interactive flag or documents the workaround.
notes: Live deploy this session: canvas-rg fully provisioned (23 resources), API/frontend health-checked 200, canvas-migrate succeeded, one real architect user (muir.jc@gmail.com) created successfully via the worked-around invocation.

title: Project physical purge after retention window
description: projects gained the identical soft-delete/retention shape as diagrams (canvas-228.2, PROJECT_RETENTION_DAYS=30, restoreProject/listDeletedProjects in project.service.ts) but jmuir-yvh's physical-purge fix scoped to diagrams only (that bead named diagrams specifically, predating canvas-228.2). A soft-deleted project past its retention window is excluded from queries and blocked from restore, but no code path ever physically deletes the row. Should mirror jmuir-yvh's approach: a findExpiredProjectIds()/purgeExpiredProjects() pair in project.service.ts, extending apps/api/src/purge/run.ts (or a sibling script) to also purge them -- an expired project should probably purge cleanly only if it already has zero diagrams/children (mirroring deleteProject's own 409 guard), which needs a decision: skip an expired-but-non-empty project silently, or purge its still-nested diagrams/children too via jmuir-yvh's own purgeExpiredDiagrams().

title: Option B: unify ProjectsPage + ProjectBrowser into one drill-in browsing surface (deferred, needs a decision)
description: Option B from docs/navigation-flow-brief.md §6 Q1 / §7 US5 — the structural alternative to the Option A epic (canvas-3vq) already in progress. Retires 'current project' as global app state entirely. A single 'Browse' screen: top level is the (searchable) project list (today's ProjectsPage content), clicking a project drills into its diagrams (today's ProjectBrowser content) with a real breadcrumb, and the header shrinks to sign-out plus at most a lightweight 'recently opened' shortcut rather than a full ProjectPicker <select>. This is the more principled long-term IA (closer to a Drive/Notion-style mental model) and would let App.tsx collapse its three near-duplicated unsaved-changes guards (requestProjectChange/requestGoHome/requestViewProjects, brief §5 Finding D) into one, since there'd only be one navigation destination. Deliberately NOT started yet — explicitly gated on a future product decision to actually pursue it, per the user's own framing when this bead was filed ('knowing that we will ultimately need to build out Option B' — acknowledged future direction, not present scope). Real work, not a same-day fix: touches App.tsx's core state model, the withProjectContext URL-carrying mechanism every admin link depends on (project-context.ts:41-53), AppShell.tsx's 'every view needs to know which project it's in' assumption (which would need a different, still-always-visible affordance once there's no single 'current project'), and the 14+ e2e specs anchored on today's default landing screen (ProjectBrowser) and today's ProjectPicker-driven project-switch flow.
design: Option A's pieces (canvas-3vq: View Diagrams action, ProjectBrowser breadcrumb, diagram search, client-side project filter) are explicitly designed to survive this later structural merge rather than being thrown away, per brief §6's recommendation. Do not start implementation until a follow-up decision explicitly greenlights Option B over continuing to iterate on Option A.
acceptance_criteria: Blocked/deferred — no acceptance criteria until the decision to pursue Option B is made and this epic is actually scoped/broken into child stories at that time.

title: Server-side project search (?q= param on GET /projects) — gated on real scale (US4)
description: US4 from docs/navigation-flow-brief.md §7 (Finding B, project-level, at scale). Symmetric work to what's already built for diagrams (searchDiagrams) — add a server ?q= param on GET /projects mirroring searchDiagrams's exact shape. NOT ready to start: gated on real (non-test-debris) project counts actually justifying it. The brief's own 380-project figure from the seeded dev DB is known to be inflated by accumulated e2e-test debris (epoch-millisecond-suffixed names like 'A11y Shared Source 1785595258420'), so it's not evidence of real organic scale. Brief §9 open question 2 suggests a rough threshold worth deciding (e.g. 'when any single user's real project count exceeds ~50') rather than leaving this open-ended forever.
design: Blocked on a product decision (the count threshold), not on any other bead in canvas-3vq — can ship independently once triggered.
acceptance_criteria: Not started until the trigger condition is actually decided. Once triggered: GET /projects accepts ?q=, filters server-side by name, ProjectsPage's client-side filter (canvas-3vq.3) is replaced or supplemented by a real query.

title: Entirely unsupported Mermaid diagram types (~24, not yet scoped)
description: 001 spec explicitly deferred these; listed here for full-roadmap visibility, not yet prioritized or broken into individual features. Full list from the Mermaid syntax reference: swimlanes, state diagram, user journey, gantt, pie chart, quadrant chart, requirement diagram, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, ZenUML, sankey, XY chart, block diagram, packet, kanban, radar, event modeling, treemap, venn, Ishikawa, Wardley, Cynefin, treeview. Split into individual per-type issues once/if prioritized — state diagram and gantt are probably the highest-value candidates given how commonly they appear in real documentation.
